speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of the skin; to determine the cause, I need to know your exact age in hours or days and when you first noticed the jaundice. Additionally, have you had any feeding difficulties or passed unusually dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice of the Newborn. The history of a 5-day-old term infant with jaundice appearing on day 4, exclusive breastfeeding, and no dark urine or pale stools is most consistent with benign physiological jaundice or early breastfeeding jaundice.
